Catalytic Transient Leaving Group for Atom-Economic Synthesis of 
Allenes from 2-Alkynols 
Wanli Zhang, 
a Chaofan Huang, b Yuan Yuan, b and Shengming Ma *b,c  
An atom economic approach from readily available pr opargylic 
alcohols to allenes, the first carboxylation of pro pargylic alcohols, 
has been established. Under the cooperative binary catalysis of Pd 
and a phosphoric acid, the reaction afforded multi- substituted 
allenoates with a broad scope tolerating useful fun ctional groups. 
Synthetic potentials of obtained products have been  
demonstrated.  
The presence of two cumulated carbon-carbon double bonds 
is the distinctive structural characteristic of all enes and 
contributes to their extraordinary reactivities. 1 Due to the 
broad existence of allene unit in natural products,  
pharmaceutical molecules, and applications of allen es in 
advanced molecules/materials, the chemistry of alle nes has 
been catching increasing attention from chemists.2,3 Especially, 
much attention has been focused on development of n ew 
methodologies for accessing differently substituted  allenes 
recently.4 In addition to the well established coupling reactions 
of alkynes with a propargylic leaving group with 
organometallic reagents, 
4 the Pd-catalyzed carboxylative 
coupling reactions of propargylic mesylates or carb onates with 
alcohols in the presence of CO afforded 2,3-allenoa tes via Int-
1.5 However, such a coupling strategy utilizing the re adily 
available 2-alkynols has never been reported due to  the 
difficulty encountered in the step of oxidative add ition of 2-
alkynols with a transition metal catalyst although the SN2'-type 
reaction of 2-alkynols with a stoichiometric amount of TiCl4 for 
the synthesis of 1,2-allenyl chlorides has been rep orted. 6 We 
would like to propose a new concept of utilizing a catalytic 
amount of Brønsted acid to form a transient leaving group  
from the hydroxy group in the readily available pro pargylic 
alcohols, which would trigger an oxidative addition  with a 
transition metal catalyst to cleave their propargyl ic carbon-
oxygen bond for subsequent coupling reactions via a  similar 
Int-1-type intermediate. The challenge is to identifying  the 
cooperative working Brønsted acid and transition me tal 
catalysts.7 Herein, we report the first Pd/H +-cocatalyzed 
preparation of tetra- or tri-substituted allenoates  from 2-
alkynols.

Scheme 1. Carboxylation approaches to 2,3-allenoates with CO 
Initially, the study was launched using 2-phenyloct -3-yn-2-ol 
(1a ) as the starting material, [(π-allyl)PdCl] 2 as the catalyst and 
BINAP as the ligand to identify the appropriate aci d. When 
CF 3COOH was added, the expected formations of enone 2a  
and enyne 3a  were detected (Table 1, entry 1): enone 2a  was 
formed through Meyer-Schuster rearrangement and 3a  was 
formed via dehydration with the help of CF 3COOH (Scheme 2). 8 
A  range  of acids were then screened, however, the  expected 
product 4a  was not formed (Table 1, entries 2-7). To our 
delight, when 1,1'-binaphthyl-2,2'-diyl hydrogen ph osphate 
(acid 4) was used, 22% yield of 4a  was detected together with 
7% yield of 3a  (Table 1, entry 8). Using Ph 2POOH led to inferior 
results-4a  was formed in only 2% yield (Table 1, entry 9). 
Surprisingly, the reaction with (PhO) 2POOH afforded 27% yield 
of allenoate 4a  (Table 1, entry 10). Control experiment was

    Encouraged by these results, different Pd source s were then 
examined. PdCl 2, PdCl 2(PPh 3)2, and  [PdCl(cinnamyl)] 2 gave 2-
21% yields of 4a (Table 2, entries 1-3). PdCl 2(DPPE) and 
PdCl2(DPPF) were ineffective-nothing but 14-21% yields o f 3a 
were detected (Table 2, entries 4 and 5). [(π-allyl )PdCl] 2 was 
the most ideal Pd catalyst, obtaining 4a  with 27% yield (Table 
2, entry 6). Running the reaction at 50 oC gave better results-a 
higher yield of 4a  with some recovery of starting material 
alcohol 1a  was observed (Table 2, entry 7). 
Ligands always play an important role in organometa llic 
catalysis. PPh 3 and P(2-furyl) 3 were able to accelerate the 
formation of allenoates, obtaining 4a  with 35-37% yields 
(Table 3, entries 2 and 3), whereas Zheda-Phos 9 led to nothing 
but 62% recovery of 1a (Table 3, entry 4). When Sphos was 
used, 30% yield of 4a  and 66% recovery of 1a  were detected 
(Table 3, entry 5). Diphosphine ligands were also i nvestigated: 
DPPE gave inferior result with 100% of 1a  being recovered 
(Table 3, entry 6); the desired allenoate 4a  was produced with 
20% yield when applying DPPF (Table 3, entry 7); fi nally, it was 
found that DPEphos was the most effective ligand, fo rming 4a 
with 64% yield (Table 3, entry 8).

Apart from these, secondary propargylic alcohol may also be 
utilized to give trisubstituted allenoates 4u with 68% yield (eq. 
1). The reaction may be easily conducted on 5 mmol scale of 
1a  (eq. 2). 
 
 
In order to unveil the mechanism of this carboxylat ion 
reaction, the reactions of 
1u  and 1u-18 O at 50 oC were 
conducted and analyzed via 1H-NMR analysis (For details, see 
Supporting Information). A linear relationship was observed 
for ln ([ 1u ]) vs. reaction time, indicating a first-order 
dependence of reaction rate with respect to substra te 1u.10  In 
addition, no 18 O was found in the product 4u . The kinetic 
isotopic effect was determined to be 1.40, indicati ng that the 
cleavage of C-O bond is not the rate-determined step (eq. 3). 
 
Based on these results, a plausible mechanism is pr oposed 
(Scheme 3): the reaction of propargylic alcohol wit h Brønsted acid 
(HB) would yield the oxonium ion I, which would eas ily undergo 
oxidative addition reaction with Pd(0) to produce t he 
allenylpalladium intermediate II. Its subsequent re action with CO 
and MeOH afforded intermediates III and/or IV while  regenerating 
HB. Although intermediate III may be more viable, 11  complete 
exclusion of intermediate IV is not possible. Subse quent reductive 
elimination would afford 2,3-allenoate products and  regenerate 
active Pd(0) catalyst to fulfill the catalytic cycl e. We reasoned that 
the acidity of (PhO) 2POOH matches the propargylic alcohols and the 
large bite angle of DPEphos (104 o) (DPPE (86 o) and DPPF (99 o))12  
accelerated the reductive elimination of intermediate III and/or IV.  
 
Scheme 3. A plausible mechanism 
As a class of useful chemicals in organic synthesis , 2,3-
allenoates can be transferred into different versat ile products 
(Scheme 4): treatment with CuBr 2 or I 2 afforded 4-bromo-
2( 5H )-furanone (5)13  or 4-iodo-2( 5H )-furanone (6)14  with good 
to excellent yields; hydrolysis with KOH at 50 oC for 1.5 hours 
afforded tetra-substituted allenic acid 7 in a nearly 
quantitative yield; 15  reduction with DIBAL-H at -78 oC could 
yield 2,3-allenol 8 with 70% yield; 1,2-addition reaction with 
allyl magnesium chloride furnished tertiary α-allenol 9 with 
85% yield.16

Scheme 4. Synthetic applications of tetra-substituted allen otae 4a 
    In conclusion, a robust and atom-economic strai ghtforward 
protocol utilizing Brønsted acid and palladium as t he catalysts 
for the preparation of multi-substituted 2,3-alleno ates from 
the readily available propargylic alcohols with mod erate to 
good yields directly was developed. The synthetic p otentials of 
these allenoates have also been demonstrated formin g other 
useful building blocks. Mechanistic study shows tha t the 
cleavage of C-O bond with the k 16 O/k 18 O of 1.40. This protocol 
would open a new area for the synthesis of allenes directly 
from propargylic alocols via the Int-1-based coupling strategy. 
Further studies in this area including the role of each catalyst 
and enantioselective carboxylation are being conduc ted in our 
laboratory.
